posts.title: UK Beer And Pubs Contributed GBP37.8bn In 2025, BBPA Says
posts.excerpt: Research commissioned by the British Beer and Pub Association puts the sector's 2025 economic contribution at GBP37.8 billion, supporting nearly one million jobs.
posts.meta_title: UK Beer And Pubs: GBP37.8bn Contribution | BevOry
posts.meta_description: BBPA research puts UK beer and pubs' 2025 contribution at GBP37.8bn. Read the jobs, tax and investment figures, and what they actually measure.
posts.selection_note: A recent industry-commissioned economic report, covered by The Brewers Journal on 7 October, with attributable figures rather than speculative sales forecasts.
posts.content:
The UK's beer-and-pub sector contributed GBP37.8 billion to the economy in 2025 and supported nearly one million jobs, according to research commissioned by the British Beer and Pub Association. The analysis was carried out by Oxford Economics. The BBPA announcement also reports GBP16.8 billion in tax contributions.

Investment Alongside The Jobs Figure

The research puts net capital investment at GBP2.2 billion for 2025. The Brewers Journal's coverage on 7 October reports that figure alongside the association's calls for business-rates reform and a beer-duty freeze.

Those calls are policy requests from the trade body, not announcements that the government has adopted them. Likewise, the report concerns 2025 activity; it is not a count of beer purchases made this week.

Economic Contribution Is Not Bottle Sales

Gross value added, or GVA, measures output after subtracting goods and services used up in producing it. The Office for National Statistics explains the distinction. GVA is not the same as turnover or company profit.

Our reading: these figures help explain the sector's place in the economy. They do not tell a drinker that every brewery is growing, every pub is profitable or an individual beer offers better value.

What It Means For An Indian Beer Buyer

This is UK industry news, not an Indian price announcement. It gives no basis for changing the quoted price of a can in Mumbai or a bottle in Bengaluru.

For your own purchase, the useful comparison remains the exact beer, its labelled volume and your city's listing. A large industry contribution and a good beer for dinner are different questions. This report addresses the first.

posts.title: Lager vs Ale: Taste, Indian Food Pairings And How To Choose
posts.excerpt: Lager and ale are not light and dark versions of beer. Understand the yeast distinction, recognise familiar styles and choose a match for dinner.
posts.meta_title: Lager vs Ale: Taste & Indian Food Pairings | BevOry
posts.meta_description: Understand lager vs ale, from pilsner to IPA and wheat beer. Find Indian food pairings and compare exact beers and city prices on BevOry.
posts.selection_note: An evergreen beer-style comparison that answers practical taste and meal questions without treating colour, strength or price as a quality ranking.
posts.content:
Lager and ale are two principal beer families distinguished by the yeast used in brewing, not by colour. Neither name, on its own, tells you how strong, bitter or expensive the beer will be. For a useful comparison, go one level deeper and look at the style.

What Yeast Changes

As WSET's beer primer explains, yeast turns sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide. Ale yeasts can add fruity or spicy flavours; lager yeasts generally make a less pronounced flavour contribution. Malt and hops still have a major say in the finished beer.

Think of ale and lager as broad directions, not ready-made tasting notes. A fruity ale need not taste sweet, and a lager need not be pale.

Four Styles You Can Recognise In The Glass

  • International pale lager: usually restrained, with bread or cracker-like malt and relatively subtle hop character.
  • Czech or German pilsner: a lager with more noticeable bitterness and floral, herbal or spicy hop notes.
  • American IPA: an ale known for pronounced hops, often citrus, pine or tropical fruit, with substantial bitterness.
  • Weissbier: a wheat-beer style whose yeast can bring banana and clove aromas.

WSET's style guide describes these differences. They are style signposts: one producer's IPA can taste quite different from another's.

Dark Beer Can Be Lager, Too

Dunkles bock is a darker lager with flavours such as bread crust, nuts and dried fruit. Colour therefore cannot settle the ale-versus-lager question. Another useful exception to simple stereotypes is Cologne's Kolsch: an ale that undergoes cold conditioning. Both appear in WSET's German beer guide.

Indian Food Pairings Worth Trying

Try a restrained pale lager with rava-fried fish or lightly spiced paneer tikka. For banana-and-clove wheat beer, start with malai paneer tikka or tandoori prawns. A malt-led darker lager is worth trying with roast chicken or mushroom kebabs.

With a bitter IPA, begin with modest chilli rather than your hottest chutney. The Brewers Association's food guide notes that hop bitterness can emphasise chilli heat. These dish matches are our serving suggestions, not guarantees that every beer will pair equally well.

Which Should You Buy?

If you want restrained flavours, look at pale lager or helles. If you enjoy assertive hops, investigate an IPA. For yeast-led banana and clove, choose weissbier. The narrower style gives you a better starting point than ale or lager alone.

For Mumbai, Delhi, Gurgaon or Bengaluru price comparisons on BevOry, match the beer name and pack size, then compare its ABV separately. A higher price does not prove that ale is superior to lager. Choose the flavour you want alongside the food you are actually eating.

posts.title: Beer Pint, Can Or Bottle? Compare 330 ml, 500 ml And 650 ml
posts.excerpt: Compare beer prices by labelled volume, not container names. Use price per 100 ml and total multipack volume to make a fair comparison.
posts.meta_title: Beer Pint, Can & Bottle Sizes In India | BevOry
posts.meta_description: Compare 330 ml, 500 ml and 650 ml beer packs, understand pint measures and calculate price per 100 ml. Check your city's exact listing on BevOry.
posts.selection_note: A practical pack-size and unit-price guide for Indian city searches; uses transparent volume arithmetic rather than invented rupee prices or discounts.
posts.content:
A fair beer-price comparison starts with the volume printed on the pack. A smaller can can cost less at the checkout while costing more per 100 ml. The words pint, bottle and can are not enough to compare two listings.

How Many Millilitres Are In A Pint?

A British imperial pint is approximately 568 ml, as the conversion table in GOV.UK's weights-and-measures guidance shows. That is a measurement conversion, not an Indian beer-pack rule.

For a packaged beer described as a pint, use its labelled millilitres. Do not automatically turn the name into 568 ml. At a bar, ask which serving volume the menu price covers.

Compare The Quantity Before The Price

For these illustrative pack sizes, the arithmetic is simple: 330 ml is 0.33 litres, 500 ml is half a litre, and 650 ml is 0.65 litres. A 650 ml pack contains roughly 1.97 times the volume of a 330 ml pack, not exactly twice as much.

These examples explain the calculation; they do not mean every beer is sold in all three sizes. Match the volume on the specific can or bottle you are considering.

The Price-Per-100-ml Calculation

Price per 100 ml = pack price divided by pack volume in ml, multiplied by 100.

Use the actual listed price for each size. Compare the same beer and city before deciding which pack has the lower unit price. A large bottle is not automatically better value, and a low unit price is not a reason to buy more than you need.

Multipacks: Count The Whole Volume

Six 330 ml containers total 1,980 ml. Four 500 ml containers total 2,000 ml. Those packs hold almost the same volume: the difference is just 20 ml.

Divide each multipack's total price by its total volume, then multiply by 100. Do not compare a six-pack's price with a single can's price. The number of containers is not the number of litres, and a multipack name does not promise a discount.

Buying In Mumbai, Delhi Or Bengaluru

Select your city on BevOry, then match the exact beer, pack volume and number of containers. Keep ABV in view too: equal volumes of different-strength beers are not the same alcohol quantity.

Use unit price to compare quantity fairly. Use flavour, strength and the amount you plan to serve to make the final choice. The calculation is helpful; it should not make the decision for you.
